title: The Yakṣa's Questions
subtitle: Mahābhārata · Vana Parva 311–315

scenes.name: The Stolen Fire
scenes.display: As the long exile waned, a deer bounded away with a Brāhmaṇa's sacred fire-sticks tangled in its antlers. The five Pāṇḍava brothers gave chase, until it melted into shadow and left them lost, and parched.
scenes.tts: As the long exile waned, a deer bounded away with a brahmin's sacred fire-sticks tangled in its antlers. The five Pahn-dah-vah brothers gave chase, until it melted into shadow and left them lost, and parched.

scenes.name: The Still Lake
scenes.display: Nakula, youngest and swift, found a still and shining lake. As he stooped to drink, a voice rose from the empty air: "This water is mine. Answer me first — then drink."
scenes.tts: Nuh-koo-lah, youngest and swift, found a still and shining lake. As he stooped to drink, a voice rose from the empty air: this water is mine. Answer me first; then drink.

scenes.name: Four Brothers Fallen
scenes.display: Heedless with thirst, Nakula drank, and fell. Sahadeva went to look for him, and fell in turn; then Arjuna; then Bhīma — each ignoring the voice, each drinking, each lying still, until four brothers lay fallen like felled trees.
scenes.tts: Heedless with thirst, Nuh-koo-lah drank, and fell. Sah-hah-day-vah went to look for him, and fell in turn; then Ar-joona; then Bee-ma; each ignoring the voice, each drinking, each lying still, until four brothers lay fallen like felled trees.

scenes.name: A Voice with No Body
scenes.display: At last Yudhiṣṭhira came, and found all four fallen. He grieved — yet saw no wound. When the bodiless voice rose again above the still water, he bowed his head: "Ask, Yakṣa. I will answer."
scenes.tts: At last Yoo-dish-teer-ah came, and found all four fallen. He grieved; yet saw no wound. When the bodiless voice rose again above the still water, he bowed his head: ask, Yuck-shah. I will answer.

scenes.name: The Questions
scenes.display: "What is swifter than the wind?" — "The mind." "What is heavier than the earth?" — "A mother." Riddle upon riddle, he answered every one. Then came the deepest: "What is the greatest wonder?"
scenes.tts: What is swifter than the wind? The mind. What is heavier than the earth? A mother. Riddle upon riddle, he answered every one. Then came the deepest: what is the greatest wonder?

scenes.name: The Greatest Wonder
scenes.display: And Yudhiṣṭhira answered: "Day upon day, the dead are borne to the House of Death — yet those who remain believe they will never die. That is the greatest wonder."
scenes.tts: And Yoo-dish-teer-ah answered: day upon day, the dead are borne to the house of death; yet those who remain believe they will never die. That, is the greatest wonder.

scenes.name: Dharma Revealed
scenes.display: The crane blazed, and shed its shape: this was Dharma, his own divine father, testing him all along. Pleased, he raised all four brothers to their feet, and granted the Pāṇḍavas a year in which no one would know their faces.
scenes.tts: The crane blazed, and shed its shape: this was Dar-mah, his own divine father, testing him all along. Pleased, he raised all four brothers to their feet, and granted the Pahn-dah-vahs a year in which no one would know their faces.
